hypotheses.statement: Removing a finding that no duty names changes no duty, and removing any other changes at least one; the only finding the crosswalk does not name is G1
The duty view cannot tell some single failures apart: at least two findings share one duty signature
Over the 19 single and 171 pair removals the duty signatures distinguish fewer patterns than the findings do (information is lost in the projection)
No duty is SATISFIED while a finding it maps is VIOLATED, in any of the 190 patterns, and the intact institution satisfies every duty

targets: findings, duties and outcomes of a synthetic institution

instrument_conditions.patterns: 19 single + 171 pair removals from a fully provisioned institution; evidence set directly (no simulation)

reproduction.world: xzr.teoo.legal (SYNTHETIC institution) and xzr.teoo.mheg (duties, crosswalk as reported, directive states)

M101.criterion: the findings with an empty signature are exactly ['G1'] and every other single removal changes at least one duty

M102.criterion: at least one group of two or more findings with the same non-empty signature

M104.criterion: 0 violations and the intact institution satisfies every duty

catalogue.source: The Minimum Guarantees of Human Legal Subjecthood, Publication Final V3.0, Chapter 6.2 (identical in the 100_POINT_EDITION and in R2 section 4: all fifteen titles and definitions compared character for character)
catalogue.note: V3.0 uses two vocabularies for the same five findings (Appendix A table: Secured/Partial/Absent/Indeterminate/Inapplicable; A.3 and 8.4 text: Satisfied/Partially Satisfied/Failed/Indeterminate/Not Applicable). R2 section 16 and this implementation use the table's.

note: results about a SYNTHETIC institution and this implementation; the twelve duties are functional summaries and their crosswalk is as reported (R16 not available); not an observation of any institution, law or person
